title: Easter and the Resurrection IQ
subtitle: How well do you know the first Easter?

questions.text: On which day of the week did Jesus rise from the dead?

options.explanation: The Sabbath was the day Jesus rested in the tomb. The resurrection came the morning after.

options.text: The first day of the week
options.explanation: All four Gospels agree the women came to the tomb on the first day of the week, which is Sunday.
Passover was tied to the crucifixion week, but the rising itself happened on the first day of the week.
Pentecost came about fifty days later, when the Holy Spirit was given.

questions.text: Who carried Jesus' cross part of the way to the place of crucifixion?

options.explanation: Mark 15:21 says the soldiers compelled Simon of Cyrene, who was passing by, to bear the cross.
Peter had already denied Jesus three times and was not the one who carried the cross.
Joseph of Arimathea gave his own tomb for Jesus' burial, but he did not carry the cross.
John stood near the cross with Mary, but Simon of Cyrene was forced to carry it.

questions.text: What was the name of the place where Jesus was crucified?

options.explanation: Gethsemane was the garden where Jesus prayed and was arrested, not where He was crucified.
Bethany was the village of Mary, Martha, and Lazarus near Jerusalem.
John 19:17 calls it Golgotha, which means the place of a skull, also known as Calvary.
The Mount of Olives is where Jesus later ascended, not the site of the cross.

questions.text: Who asked Pilate for the body of Jesus so it could be buried?

options.explanation: Nicodemus helped wrap the body with spices, but he was not the one who asked Pilate for it.
Mark 15:43 says Joseph of Arimathea went in boldly to Pilate and asked for the body of Jesus.
Mary Magdalene came to the tomb on Sunday morning, but a man named Joseph asked Pilate for the body.
Judas had already betrayed Jesus and died, so he had no part in the burial.

questions.text: What was used to close the entrance of Jesus' tomb?

options.explanation: Tombs like this were sealed with stone, not wood.
Matthew 27:60 says Joseph rolled a great stone to the door of the tomb.
There was no iron gate. The opening was blocked by a large stone.
A curtain hung in the temple and was torn at the crucifixion, but the tomb was closed with a stone.

questions.text: Who was the first person to see the risen Jesus, according to John's Gospel?

options.explanation: Peter ran to the empty tomb, but he did not see the risen Jesus first.
Thomas saw Jesus later and doubted until he was shown the wounds.
In John 20:14-16, Mary Magdalene met the risen Jesus near the tomb and He spoke her name.
The Gospels name Mary Magdalene as the first to see Him, not His mother.

questions.text: When Mary Magdalene first saw Jesus outside the tomb, who did she think He was?

options.explanation: She did not mistake Him for a soldier. She thought He worked in the garden.
Mary had already seen angels in the tomb. The man she spoke to she took for someone else.
John 20:15 says she supposed Him to be the gardener until He called her by name.
She did not think He was Peter. She mistook Him for the keeper of the garden.

questions.text: Which disciple doubted the resurrection until he saw Jesus' wounds?

options.explanation: John 20:25 records Thomas saying he would not believe unless he saw and touched the wounds.
Philip asked to see the Father earlier, but the famous doubter was Thomas.
Andrew is not the disciple who demanded to see the wounds.
Matthew was a former tax collector, but Thomas was the one who doubted here.

questions.text: On the road to Emmaus, when did the two travelers finally recognize the risen Jesus?

options.text: When He first joined them on the road
options.explanation: Luke 24:16 says their eyes were held so they did not know Him at first.

options.text: When He broke bread with them
options.explanation: Luke 24:30-31 says their eyes were opened and they knew Him as He broke the bread.

options.text: When He read from the prophets
options.explanation: He did explain the Scriptures to them, but they recognized Him only at the meal.
No angels appeared on the road. They knew Him when He broke bread.

questions.text: What did Jesus tell the women to do after they met Him outside the empty tomb?

options.explanation: He did not ask them to guard anything. He sent them to His followers.

options.text: Tell His brethren to go to Galilee
options.explanation: Matthew 28:10 says, "Go tell my brethren that they depart into Galilee, and there shall they see me" (ASV).

options.text: Bring the priests to the tomb
options.explanation: He never sent them to the priests. He sent them to His disciples.
He told them to go and tell, not to stay silent.

questions.text: How many days after His resurrection did Jesus stay with His followers before ascending?

options.explanation: Three days was the time in the tomb, not the time before the ascension.
The book of Acts gives a longer span than a week.
Acts 1:3 says He showed Himself alive over a period of forty days, speaking of the kingdom of God.
Fifty days points to Pentecost, which came after He had already ascended.

questions.text: What did the angel at the tomb tell the women about why it was empty?

options.explanation: That was a false rumor spread later. The angel said something very different.

options.text: He is not here; for he is risen
options.explanation: Matthew 28:6 records the angel saying, "He is not here; for he is risen, even as he said" (ASV).
The angel did not send them to Bethany. The message was that He had risen.

options.text: He is still in the grave clothes
options.explanation: The grave clothes were left behind, but the angel's point was that He was alive.

scoring.perfectMessage: A perfect score. You know the empty tomb by heart.

gradeBands.label: Seeker
gradeBands.message: The Easter story is waiting for you. Open the Gospels and start with the last week of Jesus' life.

gradeBands.label: Student
gradeBands.message: You know the heart of the story. A few more readings and the details will stick.

gradeBands.label: Scholar
gradeBands.message: You know the resurrection well. Strong work.

gradeBands.label: Sage
gradeBands.message: Few know the first Easter this clearly. Beautifully done.
